script: Spread and total were not saved, so this is form-only. Baltimore has been the more complete offense: Derrick Henry has 301 rush yards on 66 carries (4.56 YPC) and Lamar Jackson is +0.32 EPA/dropback vs the blitz and +0.35 without it, while Cam Ward is -0.19 EPA when not blitzed. Form points to BAL leaning on Henry's 22-carry pace plus Jackson's legs, with Tennessee throwing into a Ravens defense that has leaked on the ground (4.13 YPC, 10 runs of 10+) but allowed only 8 passes of 20+ on 112 attempts.
who_goes_off: Rashod Bateman is the Baltimore pass-game piece set up to eat: 125 receiving yards on 13 targets and 175 air yards (13.5 aDOT) into Tennessee's leaky outside zones. Tony Pollard is the Titans skill player set up on the ground: 173 rush yards on 38 carries (4.55 YPC) against a Baltimore run defense that has already allowed 10 runs of 10+ yards.
weak_spot: Baltimore's hole is the middle, not the boundary: 8.30 YPA on 23 middle attempts versus 5.34 YPA on 41 right and 6.93 on 41 left, so the matchup is linebackers, nickel, and safeties. Tennessee's leak is the opposite: left 7.30 YPA on 30 attempts and right 7.37 YPA on 38, with the middle their tightest area at 6.53 YPA on 15 attempts, plus 9 passes of 20+ allowed on 89 attempts.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for TEN@BAL, so there is no absence to reprice. Usage is the sheet itself: Henry 66 carries to Justice Hill's 13, Pollard 38 carries to Tyjae Spears' 13, and Titans targets piled on Carnell Tate (20) and Wanda Robinson (18) while Calvin Ridley does not appear in the three-game target list.
qb_vs_blitz: Cam Ward is +0.13 EPA/dropback vs the blitz (n=26) and -0.19 when not blitzed, and Baltimore blitzes 37%, so his better split is the one he will see more — short and middle answers (Gunnar Helm 11 targets, Wanda Robinson 18) matter when five rushers come. Lamar Jackson is +0.32 vs the blitz (n=31) and +0.35 without it; Tennessee blitzes only 21%, so his efficiency does not depend on pressure and the 127 rush yards on 14 carries read as designed volume more than scramble variance.

picks.why: Bateman is at 41.7 receiving yards per game (125 on 13 targets) against a 27.0 line, with 175 air yards marking him as the vertical outside piece. Tennessee allows 7.30 YPA left and 7.37 right and has given up 9 gains of 20+ on 89 attempts, so 27 sits about 15 yards under both his pace and the side of the field he attacks.

Pollard is at 57.7 rush yards per game on 12.7 carries and the line is 48. Baltimore allows 4.13 YPC and 10 runs of 10+; 12.7 carries times 4.13 YPC is 52.4 even if he only matches what this defense gives up, and his own 4.55 YPC over 38 carries pushes the expectation closer to 58.
